questions.question: _________ of the Constitution of India provides protection against arrest and detention in certain cases.
questions.solution:
Article 22 of the Constitution of India provides protection against arrest and detention in certain cases. it ensures that an arrested person is informed of the grounds of arrest, has the right to consult a legal practitioner, and must be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours.

Note: This article distinguishes between punitive detention (after a trial) and preventive detention (without trial to prevent a crime).

questions.question: Out of the given four alternatives, select the one that is NOT a constitutional body?
questions.solution:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) is NOT a constitutional body; it is a statutory body established under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.

Constitutional Bodies: The Finance Commission (Art 280), Election Commission (Art 324), and UPSC (Art 315) are all established directly by the Constitution of India.

questions.question: Who among the following described the Indian Constitution as ‘quasi federal’?
questions.solution:
KC Wheare described the Indian Constitution as ‘quasi-federal’. He believed that while India has federal features, it also possesses strong unitary characteristics (centralization of power).

Note: Other scholars like Granville Austin described it as 'Cooperative Federalism'.

questions.question: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution divides the power between the Centre and the state in terms of the union, state and concurrent list?
questions.solution:
The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution divides power between the Centre and the states through three lists: the Union List (100 subjects), the State List (61 subjects), and the Concurrent List (52 subjects).

Key Fact: Residuary powers (subjects not in any list) belong to the Union Parliament.

questions.question: Who has the right to appoint an inter-state council to promote centre-state and inter-state cooperation?
questions.option_3: Both the Prime Minister and Chief Minister together
questions.option_4: Both the President and Governor together
questions.solution:
The President of India has the right to appoint an Inter-State Council under Article 263 of the Constitution. The primary purpose of this council is to investigate and discuss subjects of common interest and to promote coordination between the states and the Union.

Note: The Prime Minister acts as the Chairman of this Council.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the impeachment of the President?
questions.solution:
Article 61 of the Indian Constitution deals with the procedure for the impeachment of the President. The only ground for impeachment is 'violation of the Constitution'.

Process: Charges can be initiated by either House of Parliament and must be passed by a special majority of two-thirds of the total membership of both Houses.

questions.question: Article 32 of the Constitution of India deals with the:
questions.option_1: Right to Freedom of Speech and Expression
questions.solution:
Article 32 deals with the Right to Constitutional Remedies. It allows citizens to approach the Supreme Court directly if their Fundamental Rights are violated.

Note: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar famously called this article the 'Heart and Soul' of the Constitution.

questions.question: The idea of a single citizenship in the Constitution of India was borrowed from:
questions.solution:
The idea of single citizenship in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the United Kingdom (Britain). Unlike federal systems like the US, where people have both national and state citizenship, Indians have only one citizenship regardless of their state of residence.

Purpose: To promote national integration and unity.

questions.question: A judge of the High Court retires at the age of _____.
questions.solution:
A judge of the High Court retires at the age of 62 years.

Comparison: A judge of the Supreme Court retires at the age of 65 years. There have been several legislative proposals to increase the retirement age of High Court judges to 65, but 62 remains the current constitutional limit.

questions.question: The Regional Rural Banks Act was passed in __________.
questions.solution:
The Regional Rural Banks (RRB) Act was passed in 1976. This act followed the Narasimham Working Group recommendations and was intended to provide institutional credit to the rural population, especially small farmers and agricultural laborers.

Note: The first RRB, Prathama Bank, was set up in 1975 before the Act was formally passed.

questions.question: Part III of the Constitution of India deals with:
questions.solution: Part III of the Constitution of India (Articles 12 to 35) deals with Fundamental Rights. These rights are protected and guaranteed by the Constitution as they are essential for the holistic development of individuals and the preservation of human dignity.

questions.question: In 1978, the _______ to the Constitution removed the right to property from the list of Fundamental Rights.
questions.solution: In 1978, the 44th Amendment to the Constitution removed the Right to Property from the list of Fundamental Rights. It was moved from Article 31 to Article 300A, where it now exists as a legal or constitutional right rather than a fundamental one.

questions.question: Which Part of the Indian Constitution deals with the State Legislature?
questions.solution:
Part VI of the Indian Constitution deals with the States, including the State Legislature (Articles 168 to 212). It covers the composition, duration, and powers of the Legislative Assemblies (Vidhan Sabha) and Legislative Councils (Vidhan Parishad).

Note: Part V deals with the Union (Centre).

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the definition of the Money Bill?
questions.solution:
Article 110 deals with the definition of a Money Bill. A bill is deemed to be a Money Bill if it contains only provisions dealing with taxes, borrowing of money by the government, or the Consolidated Fund of India.

Key Authority: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha has the final authority to decide whether a bill is a Money Bill or not.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding the election of Vice-President?
questions.option_1: He/she is qualified for election as a member of the Council of States.
questions.option_2: He/she has completed the age of 35 years of age.
questions.option_3: He/she must be a citizen of India.
questions.option_4: He/she is qualified for election as a member of the House of People.
questions.solution:
The statement that a candidate for Vice-President must be 'qualified for election as a member of the House of People (Lok Sabha)' is NOT correct. According to Article 66, the Vice-President must be qualified for election as a member of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha).

Common Requirements: Must be a citizen of India and at least 35 years of age.

questions.question: Which Act was enacted in India with the aim of curbing illegal trade in wildlife and derivative parts?
questions.solution: The Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 was enacted to curb illegal trade in wildlife and their derivative parts. It provides for the protection of wild animals, birds, and plants and establishes various schedules of protection based on the level of threat to the species.

questions.question: ‘All minorities, whether based on religion or language, shall have the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice’. Which article of the Constitution of India guarantees this right?
questions.solution:
Article 30 guarantees the right of minorities (religious or linguistic) to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice. It ensures that the state shall not discriminate against any educational institution in granting aid on the ground that it is under the management of a minority.

Related: Article 29 deals with the protection of the interests of minorities.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the election of the Vice-President?
questions.solution: Article 66 of the Indian Constitution deals with the election of the Vice-President. The Vice-President is elected by the members of an electoral college consisting of the members of both Houses of Parliament (both elected and nominated) through a system of proportional representation.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers a High Court to issue writs for the enforcement of the Fundamental Rights of the citizens?
questions.solution:
Article 226 empowers the High Courts to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose.

Comparison: While Article 32 gives similar power to the Supreme Court, the scope of Article 226 is wider because it can also be used for the enforcement of ordinary legal rights.
